sharedPlanRerun.note: FULLRUN_PLAN exactly as in common/fullrun.js (final hold 10 s). Stows not completed by the end of the hold are counted as the developer's own accounting does (walk-up + re-clip, ops +2).
sharedPlanRerun.verdict: Final hold 30 s instead of 10 s is a declared, neutral deviation: with the unmodified FULLRUN_PLAN avail 61.4 %, setup p90 10.9 s and ops p90 1 are unchanged; only 3 extra 9 m/s cases fail to seat within 10 s (stand 10.4–11.5 s) and get walk-up/ops 3 from the developer accounting — an artefact of truncation, not of the device.

gatedAccounting.verdict: Gated runs (6/39) enter with setup 1 s, ops 1, avail 0. That pulls setup p90 from 11.4 to 10.9 s (negligible) and is the correct avail accounting (refused launch = no footage).

envelope.def: launched runs (mean down-slope tailwind < 5 m/s), shared 12 m/s recreational carve on 15°

massBudget.note: rebuilt from components.js: cam4kNoGimbal 27 + 3 servos 7.5 + bracket 3 + avionics 10 + 4 servos 10 + wiring 5 + release 2 + 48→5 V buck 2 + supercap 5 = 71.5 g + structure 40.5 g (220 g/m² × 0.075 + pod/tail 16 + hinges 5 + hook 3) = 112 g ×1.15 = 128.8 g. Arithmetic correct; 220 g/m² for a folding EPP/carbon wing is plausible (ASSUMED); no lithium cell on board. Far below C0 250 g. Wing-fold mechanism, auto-deploy springs and pogo hook at 8 g total look light.

physics.assumption: 0.45 mm leash with two 0.12 mm-equivalent Cu tinsel conductors around a 0.17 mm Dyneema core + PU jacket, 0.27 g/m, 70 N
physics.devClaim: 1.8 Ω/m per conductor, 54 Ω loop (whole 15 m spool), 0.56 W loss (10 %), 5.5 V drop at 0.10 A
physics.evidence: Arithmetic: solid Cu Ø0.12 mm = 1.52 Ω/m at 20 °C (1.34 at −10 °C); mass 2×Cu 0.203 + Dyneema 0.022 + jacket ≈0.032 = 0.26 g/m — consistent. Tinsel conductors are foil ribbons on a textile core with less Cu cross-section and a longer helical path than a solid wire of equal envelope; UL tinsel appliance cord allows ≤0.92 Ω/m for a 6-thread conductor in a much thicker cord; a tinsel fabric ribbon ≈ 32 AWG is 0.3–0.5 Ω/m. Fitting two Ø0.12 mm-equivalent conductors + 0.17 mm core + enamel + jacket in 0.45 mm OD leaves ~0.02 mm per side for the jacket. 0.17 mm braided PE line is rated ≈70–90 N, so 70 N is credible. At 0.1 A the I²R heating is negligible; the voltage drop matters only if R is ≥5× higher.
physics.killTest: build 15 m of the 4-element line; measure OD, g/m, loop resistance at −10 °C, break load, and resistance after 10 000 reel cycles over the actual drum radius with the 3 N clutch; endurance stays ≥45 min only if loop R ≤ ~150 Ω (≈5 Ω/m per conductor)

physics.assumption: 48 V DC on the leash is safe to touch
physics.devClaim: SELV, current limiter, line-fault monitor, 48 V cut on a strike
physics.evidence: 48 V DC is inside ELV/SELV (≤60 V DC dry, ES1 in IEC 62368-1), but wet-location limits in several rules are ≈30 V DC; with wet gloves/skin (~1 kΩ) a damaged jacket gives ≈48 mA — painful, below DC fibrillation thresholds; the current limiter must act on leakage, not only on overload (0.1 A load). The thin 0.02 mm jacket is the weak point (abrasion on snow, ski edges).
physics.verdict: credible with a ground-fault/leakage detector; 24–30 V would need ~2–4× lower loop R for the same loss
physics.killTest: abrade the jacket against a ski edge / wet snow; measure leakage between conductors and to a wet glove; detector trip time

physics.assumption: line drag and visibility of the thicker 0.45 mm line
physics.devClaim: more visible and less cutting than 0.17 mm; drag modelled (Cd 1.2 × d)
physics.evidence: model.js spanLoad uses dLine 0.45 mm and 0.27 g/m, so the 2.6× drag increase is in the simulation (follow tension p95 ≤2.1 N). A 0.45 mm hi-vis line is still invisible to another skier beyond a few metres; the glider sweeps 4.2 m (p95) lateral across the piste with up to 15 m of line.
physics.verdict: credible (drag); visibility still a bystander hazard
physics.killTest: on-snow detection distance of a 0.45 mm hi-vis line by approaching skiers; sliding-line laceration test on skin simulant

physics.assumption: gyro EIS residual 8 % of camera rotation rate with airframe body rate 47–74 °/s RMS
physics.devClaim: jitter p90 2.3 °/s, blur p95 2.7 px at 1/1000 s
physics.evidence: Thumb 2 class camera (27 g, IMX586, 4K) is sold as Gyroflow-capable (post-processing); no published residual ratio. The 8 % ratio is ASSUMED; 15 % → subset max 2.9 °/s, 25 % → 4.6 °/s. Blur p95 2.7 px already exceeds the concept's own ≤2 px gate, and rolling-shutter wobble at 2.5 Hz short-period oscillation is not modelled. Stock Thumb 2 lens is ≈150°; the 90° fisheye is a custom lens (ASSUMED).
physics.killTest: fly the airframe (or tow a ballasted 0.78 m EPP wing) in 6 m/s gusty slope wind with the camera on the 3-servo mount; Gyroflow the clip and measure residual LOS rate >1 Hz and rolling-shutter wobble

physics.evidence: rebuild matches exactly (see massBudget); structure 220 g/m² ASSUMED; mechanisms (fold, auto-deploy, pogo hook, release) total 13 g look light but are inside the 15 % margin; +15 % overrun (148 g) still flies (subset avail 74 %, KE 13.4 J).
physics.killTest: weigh a built airframe with fold/deploy mechanism

physics.assumption: tailwind launch gate at a known down-slope component ≥5 m/s
physics.devClaim: below the gate the glider can follow (airspeed = rider speed − tailwind ≥ 1.15 Vs)
physics.evidence: Physics right for a 12 m/s rider (Vs 6.2/5.3 m/s with flaps), but the gate is (a) evaluated with oracle knowledge of the scenario mean wind (plan.tailKnown) and (b) independent of rider speed: in 3 m/s tailwind a 6–8 m/s rider gives airMin 0.68–0.84 Vs, snow contact (height 0.035 m), helmet distance 0.78 m and jitter 70–130 °/s (developer envelope). A wrong gate decision at 6–9 m/s gives KE 14.6–19.2 J and hook releases with 900 s walk-ups (developer tailwindGateProof).
physics.killTest: gate on estimated airspeed margin (rider speed − measured tailwind from the hip anemometer/GNSS drift) and show no snow contact/head approach for 6–8 m/s riders in 3 m/s tailwind

physics.assumption: deep-stall "parachute" drop, snow park, auto wing-deploy + sled tow + winch relaunch, snow-pull capture into the hip holster
physics.devClaim: automatic; stow standstill 8–12 s; ops 1 per run
physics.evidence: All simplified contacts with ASSUMED μ; pitch-up/tumble in the deep stall not modelled; capture = line in to 0.15 m. These carry the ops = 1 and setup ≤ 12 s claims.
physics.killTest: sled/winch relaunch from a parked fold on groomed and fresh snow (≥20 trials); snow-pull capture into the funnel at −10 °C with icing (≥20 trials); deep-stall drop tumble rate

definitionChecks.issue: denominator = rider speed > 2 m/s (not fullrun col.riding); gated runs = 0 (correct); stops/relaunch included. Riding-mask denominator is 0.7–0.8 pt lower.
artefact counted when ≥3 px length of ≥1 px-wide line overlaps the subject (criterion: ≥1 px). Strict any-length rule gives identical spot values.
brief does not fix the ensemble statistic; developer p90 of its own masked jitterHP (follow/free/winch/sled) passes at 2.28, integrator footageStability subject p90 3.40 fails.
final hold extended 10 → 30 s (declared); gated runs enter at 1 s. Both shown to be immaterial for p90 (10.9 vs 11.4 s).
arm tap only; rest-stop relaunch and lift-approach stow are automatic (geofence). Consistent with criteria if the automation works; release case counted +2 (walk + re-clip).
distance from wing-tip/nose points to the helmet only; recompute with nearest of head/chest/pelvis/feet gives the same maxima.
mean full-run hip energy over flown runs × mean filming seconds; cold 0.75, reserve 15 %; hip pack only discharges in the cold (no heater needed). Consistent with components.js.
80 mm tube for a 97 mm chord wing

findings.title: avail fails in every wind bin, not only by the tailwind gate
findings.detail: Launched-run mean 72.5 % (calm 71.9, 3 m/s 72.9, 6 m/s 73.6, 9 m/s 71.1); ensemble mean 61.4 %. The ceiling is set by launch-to-station, early stop drops and relaunch, so relaxing the gate cannot reach 80 %. The developer's own audit_response says so; the "FAIL (tailwind gate)" summary misattributes it.

findings.title: Unsafe flight inside the claimed envelope: slow rider + light tailwind
findings.detail: With a 3 m/s tailwind (below the 5 m/s gate) and a 6–8 m/s rider the glider stalls (airMin 0.68–0.84 Vs), touches the snow (0.035 m) and passes 0.78 m from the helmet; jitter 70–130 °/s. Ensemble calm_s11/s13 reach 0.85/0.90 m (concept gate ≥1.0 m). The gate must use the airspeed margin, not the tailwind alone; and it uses oracle wind knowledge.
findings.evidence: dev results.json envelope v6_tail3/v8_tail3, ensemble rows headMin, model.js plan.tailKnown

findings.title: Footage stability fails on the integrator metric and rests on an 8 % EIS residual
findings.detail: footageStability subject p90 3.4 °/s (>3) over 33 flown cases, 5 cases >3; developer jitter p90 2.28. Airframe body rate 47–74 °/s RMS; blur p95 2.7 px > own 2 px gate. EIS residual 25 % → 4.6 °/s.

findings.title: packVol 2.91 L assumes an 80 mm holster tube that cannot hold the 97 mm wing chord
findings.detail: span 0.775 m, chord 0.097 m; with a ≥100 mm tube the packed envelope is ≈4.2 L > 3 L. The holster is also the snow-pull capture funnel, so it cannot be a soft pocket.

findings.title: Rider-speed envelope is narrow
findings.detail: Follow-segment avail on 15°: 100/94/87/78/56/4 % at 6/8/10/12/14/16 m/s; expert 20° at 13 m/s 54 %; 24–28° at 14–15 m/s hook release. The ensemble (12 m/s preset) sits at the edge; faster riders are not served.

findings.title: Leash resistance 1.8 Ω/m per conductor is optimistic for tinsel in 0.45 mm OD
findings.detail: Endurance 53.6 → 50.2 / 47.2 / 42.2 min at 3.6 / 5.4 / 9 Ω/m; fails below 45 min above ≈7 Ω/m. Mass 0.27 g/m is arithmetically consistent.

findings.title: Labels inconsistent with the default design
findings.detail: index.js header, about, tagline, demo stages and the cam_panEIS scenario still say "121 g, 120° fisheye on a 1-axis servo pan"; defaults are 128.8 g, 90° fisheye on a 3-servo mount. The 90° fisheye is not the stock Thumb 2 lens (≈150°).

findings.title: 30 s final hold and gated-run accounting are declared and neutral
findings.detail: Unmodified FULLRUN_PLAN: same avail 61.4 %, setup p90 10.9 s, ops p90 1 (max 3). Setup p90 without gated runs 11.4 s.

safetyRegulatory: EU: 128.8 g privately built/C0-class → open A1; camera ⇒ operator registration (national practice also may require competency); C0 max 19 m/s (governor 14 m/s OK); follow-me within 50 m (15 m leash is a physical limit).
US: VLOS by the remote pilot while skiing is not credible without a visual observer or waiver; <250 g recreational exempt from registration but not from VLOS.
Bystanders: 15 m, 0.45 mm line sweeping 4.2 m (p95) laterally across the piste; crossing fault 3.3 N on the crosser, KE 14.5 J; laceration by a sliding line not assessed.
48 V on the line: ELV; needs leakage detection and abrasion-resistant jacket; wet-location limits ≈30 V in some rules.
Deep-stall drops at stops land 1.5–10 m from the rider on a busy piste; touchdown KE ≤5.5 J.
Tailwind gate uses oracle wind; a wrong decision gives KE up to 19.2 J (> 14.9 J).
credibleEnvelope: Recreational riders 6–11 m/s on ≤15–18° groomed slopes, mean wind ≤9 m/s from head/cross, tailwind 0 with slow riders and <5 m/s with ≥10 m/s riders; full-run usable footage ≈72 % (below 80 %) because launches and stops cost air time; footage stability conditional on EIS residual ≤10 %; packed volume likely ≈4 L.
verdict: Reproduces exactly (0 differences on all 39 cases). Judged on the shared ensemble: FAIL avail (61.4 %, 72.5 % even for launched runs), FAIL/at-risk jitter on the integrator metric (p90 3.4 °/s), likely FAIL packVol (≈4 L); pass pxMed, azRange, addedMass, bodyForce, handsBusy, setupTime, ops, keMax, endurance (thin margin on line resistance). Safety gap: slow rider + light tailwind inside the gate gives stall, snow contact and a 0.78 m helmet pass. Best of the four gliders on operations (1 action, ~11 s standstill) but not a usable solo follow-cam as specified.
